$comment: GDPR (EU 2016/679) → SOC 2 Type II Trust Service Criteria mappings. We map principally against the AICPA Privacy criteria (P1–P8) — these were specifically designed to align with GDPR-era privacy regulation — and reach into the Common Criteria (CC*) for security-of-processing (Art. 32) and breach (Art. 33/34). Vendor-management criteria CC9.2 carries the Article 28 processor work.
source: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017) — Privacy criteria GDPR-aligned cross-walk; OneTrust + Drata published GDPR↔SOC 2 mapping

mappings.rationale: Privacy notice provided at or before collection — direct expression of lawful, fair and transparent processing.
Personal information used only for identified purposes — the operationalisation of purpose limitation.
Retention bound to stated purposes.
Collection consistent with stated objectives — data minimisation in TSC form.
Access and correction requests handled — supports the accuracy principle.
Personal information retained and then disposed as defined — storage limitation.
Retained no longer than needed.
Confidentiality of personal data during collection, creation and processing.
Logical access security architecture protects integrity and confidentiality.
Accountability — COSO Principle 5 enforces accountability for internal control.
Purpose-bound use implies a defined lawful basis.
Notice precedes consent capture; supports demonstrable consent.
Notice at or before collection — directly expresses Art. 13 transparency.
Notice obligations extended to third-party-sourced data.
Access requests handled — Art. 15 right of access.
Requests addressed in a timely manner — DSAR SLA.
Corrections handled — Art. 16 right to rectification.
Erasure handled within the access/correction request workflow.
Privacy complaints / objections addressed in a timely manner.
Management establishes structures, reporting lines and authority — controller accountability framework.
Change-management controls embed data-protection-by-design into product changes.
Vendor and business-partner risks managed — processor due diligence and DPAs.
Third parties assessed for compliance with privacy commitments.
Inventory of personal-information types and collection methods — analogous to RoPA.
Logical-access security architecture.
External-threat protection.
Transmission and removal of information restricted (encryption in transit / at rest).
Detection and monitoring procedures.
Backup and recovery infrastructure supports availability of personal data.
Procedures to identify security incidents include personal-data breaches.
Incidents evaluated for impact — required to decide on SA notification.
Affected parties (incl. supervisory authority) notified of security incidents.
Affected parties (data subjects) notified of security incidents.
Unauthorized disclosures identified and communicated.
DPIA is the privacy-specific risk identification and analysis activity.
Reporting lines and authority — DPO as a designated organisational role.
Disclosures to third parties only with consent or stated purposes (covers cross-border transfer commitments).
Records of third-party disclosures supports transfer-mechanism evidence.
Communication with external parties — supervisory-authority cooperation.
